title: Lab Infrastructure & Setup
contentStatus: Draft for DiFacto review. Title and content to be confirmed.

sections.title: Infrastructure as an Instructor Responsibility
learningObjectives: Understand why lab infrastructure knowledge is part of Master Instructor competency
Recognize the distinction between delivering training and enabling the facility it happens in
sections.content: Good instruction depends on an adequately equipped training environment. A Master Instructor who can set up and validate a proper lab setup is far more valuable to DiFacto's scaling efforts than one who can only teach in a pre-built environment someone else configured. This module builds that infrastructure capability directly.

sections.title: Minimum Lab Requirements by Level
learningObjectives: Understand the proposed minimum lab specification for L2 and above
Recognize how lab requirements scale with the level being taught
sections.content: Delivering L2 and above requires, at minimum: a MoRo unit (the A-500 is proposed as the primary training unit, to be confirmed with DiFacto), ANT Server installation, Wi-Fi configured for fleet communication, adequate clear floor space for mission demonstration, a payload fixture, and safety barriers or pedestrian markings. L3A and above add further requirements - maintenance tools, spare sensor units, network switching for VLAN training, and FANUC controller access (even simulated) for integration modules.

keyTerms.note: The ANT software installed on a dedicated laptop or workstation in the lab, used to run and monitor MoRo units.
An industrial robotics manufacturer whose controllers MoRo commonly integrates with via I/O handshake.
A method of segmenting network traffic, relevant to L3A+ training that covers network configuration.

video.title: Minimum lab requirements in 30 seconds
video.transcript: Minimum lab requirements, in 30 seconds. For L2 and above: a MoRo unit. The A-500 is proposed as the primary training unit, to be confirmed. ANT Server and Wi-Fi for fleet communication. Clear floor space and a payload fixture. Safety barriers or pedestrian markings. L3A and above add tools, spares, VLAN switching and FANUC access.

sections.title: Setting Up a Training Lab
learningObjectives: Understand the general process of establishing a new training lab
Recognize validation steps before the lab is used for actual training
sections.content: Setting up a lab means more than just acquiring the required equipment. It means validating it works as an integrated environment - confirming network connectivity, testing the mapped floor space, and running through representative training scenarios before learners arrive. A lab that technically has all required components but hasn't been validated end-to-end risks disrupting an actual training session.

sections.title: Maintaining Lab Equipment Over Time
learningObjectives: Understand why training lab equipment needs its own maintenance attention
Recognize the connection to the preventive maintenance principles from L3A
sections.content: Training lab equipment, including the MoRo unit used for instruction, needs the same preventive maintenance attention covered in L3A - arguably more so. Lab equipment often sees heavier and more varied use than a typical production deployment, with multiple learners practicing the same procedures repeatedly.

keyTerms.note: Routine checks and servicing done on a schedule to prevent faults, as covered in L3A.

sections.title: Scaling to Multiple Lab Locations
learningObjectives: Understand considerations when DiFacto's instructor network operates multiple labs
Recognize the value of consistency across lab locations
sections.content: As DiFacto's training program scales across multiple sites or partner locations, consistency across labs matters. A learner certified at one lab should have had a comparable training experience to one certified at another. Master Instructors play a role in maintaining this consistency, whether setting up a new lab location or auditing an existing one against the minimum specification.

sections.title: Troubleshooting Lab Environment Issues
learningObjectives: Understand common categories of lab-specific technical issues
Recognize the added pressure of troubleshooting with learners present
sections.content: Lab environment issues - network connectivity problems, a demonstration unit behaving unexpectedly - need quick resolution, since they directly disrupt a live training session. A production issue might tolerate a slower diagnostic pace; a live session can't. Having backup plans - alternate demonstration approaches, a secondary unit - for common failure points is part of being prepared to deliver training reliably.

questions.question: Why does L5 teach lab setup, not only teaching skill?
options: An instructor who can set up and validate a lab helps DiFacto scale training
Lab setup replaces the observed delivery for some candidates
Lab setup is assessed in place of preventive maintenance knowledge
questions.feedback: Correct. Infrastructure capability extends an instructor's value beyond just teaching in a pre-built space.

questions.question: Which item is added at L3A and above, and is not part of the L2 minimum?
questions.feedback: Correct. L3A and above add maintenance tools, spare sensor units, network switching for VLAN training, and FANUC controller access (even simulated).

questions.question: What does validating a new training lab involve, beyond acquiring equipment?
options: Checking that every piece of equipment arrived and is switched on
Having the equipment supplier sign a delivery note for the lab
Confirming the whole environment works end to end
questions.feedback: Correct. End-to-end validation prevents disruption during actual training delivery.

questions.question: Why might a training unit need more preventive maintenance attention than a production unit?
options: Many learners repeat the same procedures on it, so use is heavier and more varied
Training units follow a separate maintenance guide from production units
Training units run for longer hours each day than production units
questions.feedback: Correct. Lab equipment often sees heavier and more varied use than a typical production deployment.

questions.question: Why is quick resolution particularly important for lab environment issues during a live session?
options: Lab equipment is more expensive to repair than production equipment
The issue directly disrupts a live session with learners waiting
Learners may photograph the fault and share it with other sites
questions.feedback: Correct. The presence of learners creates added pressure for quick, reliable resolution.
